chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both):

He was asked about a man who had a slave girl, and his wife annoyed him regarding her, so he said, 'She is a gift (sadaqah) for you.' He said: 'If he said that for God's sake, he must uphold it; and if he did not say it for God's sake, he has the right to take her back if he wishes.'

key_terms.يَرْجِعَ: he has the right to return/take back

ai.seo_question: Is a husband's gift of a slave girl to his wife revocable?
ai.summary: In the context of classical Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies the revocability of gifting a slave girl (nahl) based on the giver's intention, distinguishing between a gift dedicated to God (which becomes irrevocable) and a general gift (which remains revocable). This ruling highlights the importance of intent (niyyah) in determining the legal status of property transfer within the family structure. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the nuances of gift-giving (hibah) and its revocation (ruju') in Shia fiqh.
